business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Autonomous Robotic Floor Cleaners and Mowers

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, signed 30 May 1984 and in force from 1985, subject to applicable European Union law

Convention between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed 26 November 2013 and in force from 28 December 2014
France's applicable European Union treaty framework, including the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the EU Customs Union and applicable EU free-movement and establishment rules

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and corresponding regulatory provisions, including Articles R.561-1 to R.561-22 concerning customer due diligence, beneficial ownership, politically exposed persons and enhanced measures; Articles R.561-55 to R.561-63 concerning beneficial-owner declarations; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020; Decree No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020; Commercial Code, Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-123 et seq.; beneficial-owner filing through the Registre national des entreprises administered by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder certificate of incorporation or equivalent registry extract, generally issued within three months before filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or equivalent competent corporate registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the country of origin is a Hague Apostille Convention party; otherwise French consular legalization or the applicable bilateral legalization procedure

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder articles of association and current constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, notarial authority or competent governmental authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available; otherwise French consular legalization; certified French translation by a court-certified translator may be required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial-owner declaration and ownership-control chart identifying each natural person owning or controlling more than 25 percent or otherwise exercising control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder, supported by corporate registry records and competent registry documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization for underlying foreign public documents; signature certification or notarization where required by the filing agent or origin law

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each proposed manager, legal representative and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent identity authority in the country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy; apostille or consular legalization only where specifically required by the receiving authority, bank or notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Residential address evidence for each manager, legal representative and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, governmental authority or other recognized issuer in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy, with apostille or consular legalization where required by the filing intermediary or receiving institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for French incorporation, legalization and filing actions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed shareholder, manager or authorized corporate representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization where required; Hague Apostille or French consular legalization for execution outside France, followed by certified French translation where necessary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Apply the French Monetary and Financial Code and EU AML framework; identify domestic and foreign PEPs, family members and known close associates; screen all shareholders, managers, authorized signatories, intermediaries, banks, suppliers and beneficial owners against UN Security Council lists, directly applicable EU sanctions, French national restrictive-measures data and commercially reliable sanctions databases including OFAC lists as a risk-control measure. Resolve name matches using date of birth, nationality, address and corporate identifiers. Prohibit dealings with persons subject to applicable asset freezes and escalate PEP, sanctions, adverse-media, opaque ownership, unexplained wealth and high-risk-jurisdiction indicators for enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence. Retain AML records for the statutory period, generally five years after termination of the relationship or completion of the transaction, subject to applicable extensions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre national des entreprises and applicable commercial register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the constitutive documents and filing in a legally acceptable form. French Latin script is normally used for the registered name; foreign words and transliterations may be used if not misleading, contrary to public order, or confusingly similar to an existing protected name. The name must not infringe trademarks, trade names, domain names, prior corporate names or protected geographical indications. A SARL must use the legal-form designation or an accepted abbreviation such as SARL in the statutory name or filing presentation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Governmental or ministerial titles and insignia
Any term implying a regulated financial, legal, accounting, insurance, medical, educational or governmental activity without the required authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not generally provide a statutory company-name reservation period equivalent to a formal 30-day reservation certificate. Treat 30 days as an operational hold period only, subject to availability and no third-party intervening rights. Before filing, conduct INPI, Registre national des entreprises, trademark, domain-name and trade-name searches. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects the filing, obtain the written reason, correct the name or supporting documents and resubmit through the portal. If the decision is maintained, submit a reasoned request for rectification to the competent registry or INPI channel and, where legally available, challenge the administrative decision before the competent administrative court within the applicable procedural deadline. A trademark opposition or civil action may be required separately for third-party intellectual-property objections.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A domiciliation or virtual-office arrangement may be used for the registered office if it complies with Commercial Code Articles L.123-11-1 et seq., the domiciliation provider is authorized where required, the company has a valid domiciliation contract and the premises can receive legal correspondence. It is not adequate as the sole operational footprint for manufacturing, warehousing, product testing, importation, after-sales service or regulated product compliance. A robotic-appliance business should maintain appropriate French or EU premises, logistics arrangements, records, personnel or outsourced operational controls, and evidence of actual commercial activity. Banks, tax authorities, customs authorities and AML-regulated intermediaries may reject a purely virtual profile as insufficient substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official nationwide probability is published. For a newly incorporated SARL engaged in appliance manufacturing, importation or distribution, the baseline risk of an unannounced physical inspection during the first year is qualitatively low but non-zero; an internal planning estimate of 5-10 percent is appropriate only as a non-statutory risk assumption, not as an official statistic. The risk increases materially where the registered office is virtual, VAT or customs activity is significant, product-safety issues arise, filings are inconsistent, or AML and beneficial-owner information is incomplete.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee; estimate based on approximately EUR 37.45 converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.09

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial registry or INPI registration system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee; estimate based on approximately EUR 19.33 converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.09

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory legal-notice publication for formation of the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or regulated tariff, depending on department and notice length

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French corporate-law review, formation documents and filing coordination

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign registry extracts, constitutional documents and identity materials
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French court-certified translator or qualified translation provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, commonly calculated by page, word count and certification requirements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille or French consular legalization of foreign documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary, competent apostille authority, foreign ministry or French consular authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fees plus local courier and document-handling charges; actual cost depends on document origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation for the initial incorporation period
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, commonly EUR 50-100 per month excluding optional mail-forwarding services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution or notary holding the capital deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: SARL has no statutory minimum capital requirement; EUR 1 is legally possible, but commercially adequate capitalization is recommended

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial substance, product-compliance and import-readiness review for robotic appliances

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; excludes testing, certification, customs duties, VAT, warehouse costs and ongoing compliance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-36 governing sociétés à responsabilité limitée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing commercial registration; Articles 1832 et seq. of the Civil Code governing companies generally.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre National des Entreprises and the competent Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés maintained by the relevant commercial court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-formation formalité submitted through the Guichet unique, comprising the signed SARL articles of association, declaration of beneficial owners, proof of registered office, capital-deposit certificate, and publication notice in an authorized legal-announcement medium.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required; the capital may be EUR 1 or more. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations, which issues the capital-deposit certificate. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed at incorporation unless the statutory valuation rules permit otherwise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The managers of [Company Name], a société à responsabilité limitée, resolve that: (1) the Company accepts and adopts its registered office at [full address]; (2) the subscribed capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] shares of EUR [nominal value] each, is approved, and the cash contributions are acknowledged as deposited under the applicable certificate; (3) [name] is appointed gérant for the statutory term, with authority to represent and bind the Company within the limits of French law and the articles; and (4) the gérant is authorized to complete registration, banking, tax, beneficial-owner, and administrative formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Structure and Reserve Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises and INPI trademark and company-name search services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SARL form, shareholder identities, capital, share allocation, management powers, business purpose, accounting year, and registered office. Search for conflicting company names and trademarks. Obtain written consent from the registered-office provider where the premises are not owned by the company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the company name, business purpose, address, or identity data before submission; obtain a replacement domiciliation certificate if the registry rejects the address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the articles of association. Open a provisional capital account, transfer the required cash contribution, and obtain the capital-deposit certificate. Foreign corporate shareholders should provide legalized or apostilled corporate extracts, constitutional documents, ownership-chain evidence, and certified French translations where requested.
required_dossiers: Manager declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Apostilles, legalizations, and French translations where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank compliance queries, provide missing source-of-funds or ownership documents, correct subscription amounts, and obtain a reissued deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized journal of legal announcements in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the mandatory incorporation notice to an authorized service de presse en ligne or journal d'annonces légales. Verify that the notice states the company name, form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, manager identity, and registration details required by French law. Retain the publication certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected or replacement notice and upload the corrected publication certificate if the registry identifies an incomplete or inaccurate announcement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic formation filing, select SARL, complete the company, shareholder, manager, activity, tax, establishment, and beneficial-owner fields, upload all supporting documents, sign electronically, pay the applicable registry charges, and submit the filing. The INPI transmits the data to the competent RCS registry and other relevant administrations.
required_dossiers: Manager declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Foreign-document legalizations and French translations where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI dashboard, respond within the stated deadline to registry requests, replace defective documents, correct electronic fields, and resubmit the formalité. A refusal may be challenged or cured through the competent registry procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI, Service des impôts des entreprises, social-protection authorities, and the company's selected bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the registration extract and verify the SIREN, SIRET, RCS, NAF, and VAT information. Convert the provisional capital account into the operating account, register for VAT and corporate tax where applicable, enroll employees with the required social bodies, and activate accounting, invoicing, and beneficial-owner compliance controls.
required_dossiers: VAT-option or intra-Community VAT documentation where applicable
Employment and payroll registrations where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of registry or tax data through the relevant administration, submit missing VAT or social registrations, and suspend affected operations until mandatory registrations are confirmed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No universal manufacturing licence is required for robotic vacuum appliances. Where the facility falls within the Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) nomenclature, the competent authority is the Préfet of the department, supported by the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), or DRIEAT in the Île-de-France region.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general operating licence; conditional ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization under the applicable ICPE nomenclature and facility activity thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, acting through the competent Préfecture and DREAL or DRIEAT
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA solely because of appliance assembly; classification depends on facility size, storage volumes, surface treatment, combustion equipment, solvents, batteries, waste, and other ICPE criteria. A full environmental authorization and environmental assessment may be required for qualifying installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single appliance-manufacturing threshold applies nationally. Wastewater must comply with applicable municipal discharge authorization and Water Code requirements; air emissions and VOCs must comply with applicable ICPE prescriptions and, where relevant, EU industrial-emissions or solvent rules. Hazardous and electrical waste must be segregated, documented, transferred to authorized operators, and tracked through Trackdéchets where required. Finished products must comply with applicable EU rules, including electrical safety, electromagnetic compatibility, RoHS, WEEE, REACH, Ecodesign, and battery obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupation, obtain applicable municipal planning and premises approvals, maintain fire-safety systems and emergency access, and complete fire-risk review with the local Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours where required. Structural floors, racks, lifting equipment, and production installations must be suitable for their intended loads and inspected under applicable French rules. The employer must prepare the required single occupational-risk assessment document, implement workplace safety measures, arrange statutory inspections for regulated equipment, and comply with Labour Code requirements; no general pre-opening occupational licence applies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: The competent authority is the French Directorate-General of Public Finance (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), acting through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). The principal online portal is impots.gouv.fr. Company formation and registration data are filed through the INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, which allocates or confirms the SIREN and SIRET identifiers. Foreign businesses without a French establishment generally deal with the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE), subject to the applicable transaction profile.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL obtains its SIREN, SIRET and APE activity code through the INPI Guichet unique registration process. The DGFiP then assigns the corporate income tax account and VAT account. The French VAT identification number generally consists of the country prefix FR, a two-character key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment must submit the applicable registration request to the SIEE before undertaking transactions requiring French VAT registration, including relevant domestic supplies, imports, intra-Community acquisitions or taxable services. The application should include constitutional documents, foreign tax registration evidence, proof of business activity, identity and authority documents for representatives, French business or customs details where applicable, bank information where requested, and transaction-flow documentation. Customs operations additionally require an EORI number obtained through French customs or the EU customs registration process. VAT registration does not replace EORI registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Subject to statutory conditions, an SARL may elect temporary taxation under the income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, IR), generally for up to five financial years, if it satisfies the qualifying ownership, size, age and activity requirements. A qualifying family SARL may elect IR taxation without the same five-year limitation, subject to the family-company conditions. France has no United States-style general check-the-box election for SARLs. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework may deny deductions or impose inclusion where an arrangement produces a deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcome.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), integrated with the European Union VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For businesses eligible for the French VAT exemption based on the franchise en base regime, the principal 2025 threshold for supplies of goods is EUR 85,000, with a higher tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500 subject to statutory conditions. A business exceeding the applicable threshold, making transactions excluded from the franchise, importing goods, or undertaking intra-Community transactions may require VAT registration irrespective of the domestic franchise threshold. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold applies to specified intra-Community distance sales and certain electronically supplied, telecommunications, broadcasting and electronic services, rather than serving as a general French domestic registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory electronic invoicing and transaction reporting through accredited private electronic invoicing platforms (plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires, PDPs). From 1 September 2026, all French-established businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; issuance obligations begin on 1 September 2026 for large and intermediate-sized enterprises and on 1 September 2027 for small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises. Transaction reporting (e-reporting) will apply to specified business-to-consumer and cross-border transactions. France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance requirement for ordinary domestic B2B transactions. Invoices must use the mandated structured data formats and be transmitted through the permitted platform architecture. Public-sector invoices are generally submitted through Chorus Pro. Fiscal stamping is not generally required for ordinary French VAT invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT where the exporter is able to prove exportation and exit from the EU customs territory, normally through the customs export declaration and electronic exit confirmation. The exporter must retain a consistent audit trail linking the invoice, goods, transport documents, customs declaration and exit evidence. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for VAT exemption rather than domestic export zero-rating when the customer has a valid VAT identification number in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, and the supplier satisfies reporting and documentary requirements. Services are generally outside the scope of French VAT or exempt under the applicable place-of-supply rule when supplied to a business established outside France or outside the EU, subject to customer-status, service-type and use-and-enjoyment requirements. Export VAT refunds require valid invoices, customs and transport evidence, proper VAT returns, and absence of prohibited or unsupported input VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French or EU customs export declaration containing the applicable export procedure and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory or equivalent customs export evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, Incoterms and VAT treatment
Packing list and product or serial-number records where relevant for robotic appliances
Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note or other transport document
Purchase order, sales contract and proof linking the shipment to the export invoice
Import or customs documentation in the destination country where available

Proof of payment or other commercial settlement evidence where required to corroborate the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory prerequisite because France has no general foreign-exchange repatriation control
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Export VAT exemption or refund may be reassessed if customs exit, transport, customer status, invoice linkage or transaction reality is not substantiated. Reassessed VAT may include statutory late-payment interest, generally 0.20% per month, and penalties of 10% for late or deficient payment, 40% for deliberate failure, or 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abusive conduct, subject to the facts and procedural rules. Fraudulent VAT claims can also result in criminal tax-fraud proceedings, with imprisonment and fines that may be increased for aggravated conduct. Unsupported input VAT refunds may be recovered, and improperly exempted output VAT may be assessed retrospectively with interest and penalties. Customs duties, import VAT and customs penalties may additionally apply where export or customs declarations are inaccurate, incomplete or fraudulent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (Treasury Directorate) as the competent French authorities for external financial transactions, balance-of-payments statistics, and capital movement compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under the EU Treaty framework with full convertibility for the euro. Current account payments and invisible transactions are unrestricted within the EU/EEA and with the majority of OECD and treaty partners. Capital account operations are generally liberalized, and profit remittances, dividend distributions, and intercompany capital repatriations by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders are freely executable, subject only to tax withholding where applicable and transaction-level AML scrutiny. There is no prior licensing regime for standard trade financing or investment flows involving compliant jurisdictions; however, specific prior authorizations apply to non-cooperative jurisdictions, sanctioned entities, and sensitive defense-related sectors. All material cross-border capital flows of €300,000 or above trigger an ex-post statistical declaration to the Banque de France as part of corporate balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose mandatory export proceeds surrender or statutory conversion requirements. Exporters may retain receivables in foreign currency or euro without forced repatriation timelines or minimum conversion ratios. The obligations are limited to statistical reporting of foreign receivables/payables to the Banque de France under the balance-of-payments regime and, where applicable, to the customs declaration obligation for physical cross-border cash or negotiable instruments exceeding €10,000. All export receipts may be held in foreign-currency accounts at an authorized bank or converted on the interbank market at commercial rates, subject to internal treasury policy and information required for sanctions screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.practical_treasury_implication: An FR SARL in the robotic vacuum appliance sector may settle export invoices in EUR or non-EUR currencies, maintain multi-currency treasury accounts, and avoid mandatory conversions, while maintaining full traceability for Audit and AML purposes through the banking counterparty's reporting channels.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: European digital EMI/neobank platforms registered with the ACPR under the EU e-money passport are feasible for routine euro operational flows and small payment transactions, rating Medium for day-to-day treasury settlements. Viability as the sole corporate treasury vehicle is Low because these institutions cannot legally provide documentary trade credit, commercial letters of credit, or foreign-exchange forward lines, and may terminate non-resident relationships without immediate escalation. They are also generally unsuitable for holding committed capital escrow balances where the onboarding bank must provide a domestic banking license and systemic protection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for standard low-risk SARLs manufacturing smart home appliances where the statutory managers and the ultimate beneficial owners are identified through electronic identification and a live video interview; physical attendance at a French branch is not mandatory. Nevertheless, certain banks may require an in-person meeting for non-EU directors, or a notarized and apostilled corporate dossier, regardless of the SARL's shareholding structure. The corporate Kbis extract, signed statutory deeds, proof of registered office, and original passports are mandatory baseline documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU ultimate beneficial owner holding more than 25 percent of the SARL with no audited financial history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized register of direct and indirect shareholdings; corporate charter and chain-of-ownership diagram; audited financial statements of the beneficial owner for the last two years; certificate of good standing from home jurisdiction; evidence of lawful source of funds; bank reference letters from existing regulated bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International sales to high- or elevated-risk markets or to distribution hubs requiring courier/warehousing in neighboring jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed customer due-diligence files; commercial invoices and Incoterms declarations; bill of lading and customs entry proof; end-user and end-use certificates particularly for motors, batteries, laser sensors, or navigation chips; any applicable dual-use control assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency inbound funds from a French parent account with low share capital and high cyclically fluctuating revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The SARL's statutory financial statements, cash-flow forecast, creditor ageing reports, proof of underlying sales contracts with recognized appliance distributors, and a corporate treasury policy confirming segregation of client funds from operating expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequency of wire transfers to/from multiple non-EU manufacturing suppliers or unexplained returns from third-party logistics entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier master files; master services and OEM agreements; purchase orders matching wire payments; tariff classification notes; evidence of reciprocal goods receipt; anti-fraud statement and internal escalation framework.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-EU parent or investor capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 to a French SARL operational account, with remittance information populating either the EU Regulation 2015/847 transaction reference or the French balance-of-payments motif code D017 for inward direct investment. The account bank must receive a board-approved capital injection resolution, the updated share register, proof of identity of the funding entity, and beneficial ownership declarations. EURO-denominated intra-EU shareholder contributions can alternatively be executed through SEPA Credit Transfer with purpose code E002, although cross-border capital injections above EUR 1,000,000 are regularly subject to enhanced vetting and may require the underlying transaction title, share sale documentation, and certificates of non-political exposure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for trade disbursements are cleared primarily via SWIFT MT103 for open-account transactions and via Commercial Irrevocable Documentary Letters of Credit issued by the French bank and transmitted through SWIFT MT700/MT710 for large OEM batches. EUR-denominated payments inside the EU use the SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) rail where immediate finality is needed. All disbursements must carry a valid purpose code corresponding to the commercial nature of the underlying invoice, and where the beneficirary is located in a restricted jurisdiction, prior checking against the EU sanctions list and the French DGT licenses is mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD forward foreign exchange contracts with maturity up to 24 months for conversion of export proceeds
EUR/USD foreign exchange swaps for periodic liquidity conversion alignment with the rolling cash-flow forecast
European-style EUR/USD FX options struck to protect minimum net export margins
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term intercompany borrowings denominated in non-EUR currencies
Authorized multi-bank basket forwards on EUR versus CNY, USD, GBP, and JPY executed through an ACPR-regulated bank under ISDA documentation
EMIR-reportable FX transaction on standard deliverable basis; non-deliverable forwards are not permissible for the euro as a fully freely deliverable currency
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_concentration_and_risk_control: The treasury blueprint for the FR SARL should hold operating liquidity in EUR at a tier-one domestic commercial bank, maintain a separate GBP/USD collection account only where invoicing is currency-differentiated, and use a committed intercompany credit line from the non-EU parent via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA to smooth, peak export-season procurement spikes. All FX hedges must be documented under an ISDA Master Agreement where counterparties are French or EU banks, confirmed by matching export exposure, and monitored under the SARL's internal policies to prevent speculative transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of each fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 July for a fiscal year ending 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit exposes the manager to a maximum fine of EUR 4,000 and personal civil liability; after formal notice with no rectification, the registry may initiate compulsory strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Déclaration Annuelle de Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, integrated with the RCS and Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual accounts deposit each year; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccuracy may incur a criminal fine of EUR 7,500 for a legal representative and EUR 375 per false entry, plus possible imprisonment in aggravated cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Liasse Fiscale, Form 2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing by 3 May following a 31 December fiscal year-end (non-calendar year-end: within 3 months of year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing sustains a 5% surcharge plus 0.2% per month of delay, interest at 0.2% per month, and possible assessment by tax authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Business Tax Return (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises – CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return and payment due on 15 December of the taxing year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an automatic 5% penalty plus 0.2% per month; unpaid balances may be recovered by distraint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting (AGO) Records and Dividend Tax Reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary General Assembly must be held and recorded within 6 months of fiscal year-end; dividend declarations require immediate tax reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No public filing fee; but absence of legal approvals may void dividend decisions and expose directors to liability for restitution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) for a SARL when two of three thresholds are exceeded: total balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000; net revenue > EUR 8,000,000; average staff > 50. Mandatory also if the SARL controls or is controlled by a company whose overall group exceeds these thresholds, or if specifically requested by shareholders holding at least one-third of the capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (PCG), implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; listed groups may use IFRS, but a private SARL generally applies local French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation when no change occurs; the obligation arises on any change in beneficial ownership (within 30 days) and is supplemented by the annual accounts deposit which triggers verification of RCS records. Any shareholding transfer that modifies beneficial control must be filed using the M2 form and the DBE within 30 days, without waiting for the annual cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)
Register of Directors (Registre des Décisions des Dirigeants)
Minute Book (Registre des Procès-Verbaux d'Assemblées et Décisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 320 – USD 850 per year for commercial domiciliation services in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 – USD 16,000 per year for a small to mid-sized SARL manufacturing robotic vacuum appliances

Additional innovation tax credit (Crédit d'Impôt Innovation, CII) of up to 20% on eligible innovation expenses, and research tax credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche, CIR) of 30% up to €100 million R&D base. For micro enterprises (

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally, the corporate income tax return (Form 2065-SD and associated schedules) must be filed no later than the second working day after 1 May following the close of the fiscal year, i.e., typically by 3 May for calendar-year taxpayers. For fiscal years ending on a date other than 31 December, the deadline is the second working day after 30 April of the year following the close of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification details: corporate name, SIREN/SIRET number, registered address, legal form (SARL), APE code (e.g., 2750Z for manufacture of household appliances, or 2814Z / 2829Z for machinery), tax ID (n° de TVA intracommunautaire), fiscal year start and end dates, and company registration (RCS) details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident entity operating through a French permanent establishment must use the PE's French registration (SIRET) and local address; the non-resident parent's jurisdiction and Tax ID should be declared in the appropriate identification boxes with the PE status clearly indicated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit before statutory offsets, derived from accounting profit (comptabilité) adjusted by Article 209 B and 212 bis re-integrating provisions, depreciation recapture, non-deductible expenses (e.g., fines, excessive director compensation) and deducting specific provisions and carry-forward losses. The result corresponds to box CL for ordinary profit or box CG for capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French PE must compute attributable arm's length profit based on Article 209 I of the French Tax Code (FTC); the enterprise must allocate true profits to France consistent with the OECD-authorised approach, including a fair share of executive overhead where PE-support services are provided, while transfer pricing documentation must substantiate the allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Original losses deductible under Article 209, first sentence of the FTC: 100% of the tax result for the year up to €1 million, plus 50% of the portion exceeding €1 million, with a 5-year time limit (or claimable as carried-back deficit,
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French PE may offset only losses attributable to the PE and computed under French tax rules; parent-company foreign losses are not available. Losses must be economically linked to the French activity and supported by PE accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065-SD / Crédit d'impôt recherche (Research tax credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIR (Article 244 quater B FTC): credit of 30% on eligible research expenses up to €100 million and 5% above; expenses include wages of research personnel, depreciation on R&D assets, subcontracting costs to approved public/private research bodies. Unused credits are refundable after 3 years, or immediately for young SMEs (JEI), or as a carry-forward against future CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE claiming CIR must perform eligible R&D activities in France through French establishments; personnel and assets must be physically located in France; the PE must be the taxpayer. Demonstrable operational substance and contemporaneous R&D documentation are required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065-SD / Impôt sur les sociétés calcul (CIT computation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of gross CIT at 25% (or 15% reduced rate on first €42,000 of profit for eligible SMEs), followed by the deduction of tax credits (CIR, CII) and the application of the minimum corporate income tax (
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE is subject to normal CIT on its French taxable profit; no reduced SME rate unless the French PE is a legally separate small company; the 3% social surcharge applies where the PE's parent group meets the size thresholds, irrespective of the PE's local revenue, under Article 235 ter ZC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annexe 2065-SD / Régime fiscal du siège (Head-office tax status)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attestation of the head-office's tax residence in a treaty country; confirmation of the absence of abusive tax sheltering through Article 209 B (transfer of profits to a related foreign entity subject to preferential tax regime); list of foreign permanent establishments and their results, where the option for worldwide taxation (régime mondial) is exercised.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the French entity is directly owned by a non-resident parent, the declaration must identify any activities conducted outside France for the account of the French PE; any profit shifting to a non-cooperative jurisdiction (État non coopératif) will trigger a 25% deemed-distribution withholding tax (Article 238 A) and non-deductibility of expenses paid to that jurisdiction (Article 238 A 0 bis).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065-SD / Déclaration de résultats (Tax result signature)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the legal representative and, where applicable, by the chartered accountant (expert-comptable), together with the electronic signature and date of filing. The return must be accompanied by financial statements (liasse fiscale) and any group integration schedules if the SARL is a member of a tax-consolidated group (régime d'intégration fiscale).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must be represented by a tax representative in France having an individual tax ID; the representative signs the electronic filing in his or her capacity; the power of attorney must be filed with the tax authorities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% statutory late-payment increase (majoration) on the unpaid CIT, plus a 5% late-filing penalty for submission after the statutory deadline, increasing by 0.4% per month of additional delay (capped at 10% for active taxpayers). Interest for late payment (intérêts de retard) of 0.20% per month on unpaid amounts. For omitted or inaccurate declarations, formal notice triggers a 40% bad-faith penalty (de mauvaise foi) on additional assessed tax, rising to 80% for fraudulent behaviour (manœuvres frauduleuses) under Article 1729 of the General Tax Code (CGI). Automatic imposition of a €150 minimum penalty for failure to file certain annexes (e.g., transfer pricing documentation). Where the taxpayer fails to file despite reminders, the tax authorities may impose a summary assessment and initiate criminal proceedings for tax evasion (fraude fiscale).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Article 119 bis 2 of the French General Tax Code (CGI) for dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders from France, unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable double tax treaty and provided certain conditions (e.g., EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or treaty rate) are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty is obtained either ex ante (via a reduced withholding certificate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for royalties paid by a French debtor to a non-resident is 33.33% plus social surcharges (33.33% under Article 1675 of the CGI for patent royalties and similar IP rights, with the final withholding rate being 33.33% for various intellectual property income); however, for income received by a French licensed company and passed on to a non-resident, the payment is subject to the 33.33% rate unless a treaty reduces or exempts it. transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400,000 (annual net turnover) for the obligation to maintain simplified transfer pricing reporting (

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Voluntary, intentional omission of taxable turnover, concealment of funds invoiced to French or EU distributors, deliberate under-declaration of French sales via offshore shell invoicing, false accounting documentation, creation of fictitious expenses, or conscious failure to file the Form 2065-SD and liasse fiscale within the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to €500,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years (Article 1741 CGI); fines may be increased to 75% of the evaded tax in administrative penalties, i.e. a 40% bad-faith penalty plus 80% fraud penalty, plus interest of 0.20% per month. In aggravated circumstances (e.g., carrying out transactions through a fictional intermediary or an entity established in a tax-haven (Article 1741-1 CGI)), penalties increase to €1,000,000 and 7 years' imprisonment. The court may order publication of the judgement and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A SARL manager (gérant) may face criminal conviction, personal fine, confiscation orders and imprisonment. The corporate veil may be pierced where the manager's bad faith or gross misconduct caused the tax offence under Article 1840 CGI (solidary liability for fines and penalties), and the tax administration can seek the manager's personal liability for the company's unpaid taxes and penalties if the company was used as a mere instrument of fraud. Travel bans (interdiction de gérer) are available as a complementary sanction under Article 131-46 of the French Criminal Code (up to 5 years).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Transfer Pricing (Abus de prix de transfert)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate pricing of related-party transactions (e.g., purchase of components from a related Hong Kong supplier or contract manufacturing services) at a non-arm's length price so as to shift French profits offshore; failure to file Form 2257-SD or to provide Local File / Master File; operating a French SARL without economic substance (invoice hub structure) because profits are transferred to low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax recharacterisation under Article 57 CGI on the entire shifted profit, plus a 20% penalty on the recharacterised amount (40% if the failure is deliberate); additional corporate income tax at 25% on the upward adjustment; late-payment interest; and a non-deductibility penalty for payments made to related parties in non-cooperative jurisdictions (Article 238 A 0 bis) at 25% of the amounts paid. Failure to produce TP documentation attracts a specific €150,000 penalty per documentation item; refusal to answer requests may lead to the rejection of direct evidence and assessment from the administration's own information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant or managing director who knowingly signed false transfer pricing declarations or contributed to a transfer pricing manipulation may be held jointly liable for the former entity's tax liabilities and penalties under the general concept of managerial fault (faute de gestion). If the pricing abuse also constitutes fraud under Article 1741, the manager can incur imprisonment and a personal fine. In extreme cases, the director's personal assets may be seized, and a travel ban or prohibition from conducting commercial business can be imposed by criminal courts. Tax collection can be enforced against directors where the company was insolvent and the abuse was intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the smart appliance business to conceal the origin or movement of funds: e.g., receiving cash or online payments in France and disguising them as intercompany loans, passing illicit payments through foreign shell companies or cryptocurrency rails, deliberately issuing false invoices to Chinese OEM suppliers, or commingling personal assets with corporate assets to disguise criminal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering (Article 324-1 of the French Criminal Code) is punishable by 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of €375,000 (up to €750,000 where the predicate offence is tax evasion), with additional penalties including confiscation of goods, proportional fines (up to one half of the laundered amount), professional interdiction, and the dissolution of the corporate body. Administrative sanctions under the Anti-Money Laundering/Terrorist Financing (LCB-FT) framework are also available to supervisory bodies, including warnings, injunctions and fines up to €100,000 for natural persons and €1,000,000 for legal persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal conviction of the gérant/director in his or her personal name: imprisonment up to 10 years for aggravated money laundering (Article 324-2) and a fine up to €750,000; confiscation of personal property; loss of civic rights and a prohibition to direct a company for up to 15 years; prohibition to reside in France if the director is a non-resident foreigner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Abuse of law and absence of substance)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining a French SARL as a letterbox or shell entity with no real French management, no premises, no employees and no actual manufacturing or logistical activity, while contracts and decisions are taken abroad; exploiting the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a double tax treaty by routing dividends or royalties from France without substance and without any business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell company can be held personally liable for the taxes of the legal entity if they used the company as a conduit for a fraud scheme (especially under Article L 267 of the Book of Tax Procedures: liability of directors for tax debts when the company committed tax fraud). The court may additionally impose travel bans, professional bans, confiscation of personal assets and a personal criminal fine. If the director is a foreign resident of a treaty country, the Ministry of Justice may request his or her extradition or enforce French criminal sanctions, and, where convicted, the personal sentence can include the order to reside (interdiction de séjour) in France for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Repatriate Profits / Hidden Dividend Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accumulating French profits without distribution to the non-resident owner, financing the owner's overseas lifestyle through informal loans, or distributing dividends to a non-resident parent without fulfilling the statutory withholding tax and beneficial ownership requirements; alternatively, concealing dividend payments by structuring them as excessive management fees, transfer prices, or
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French tax administration can deem unrecorded distributions as taxable dividends subject to the 25% withholding tax (Article 119 bis CGI) plus late-payment interest; the deemed distribution is assessed against the beneficial owner, and where received by a non-cooperative shareholder, the rate rises to 75%. Excessive charges to a related entity may be recharacterised as constructive dividends and disallowed, attracting a 40% bad-faith penalty. In addition, failure to file the annual statement of non-resident beneficiaries (Form 2561 bis) triggers a penalty of €150 per omission, capped at €10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be personally assessed under Article L 267 for corporate tax debts, including the withholding tax, if he or she deliberately failed to file and pay it. Criminal exposure arises if the non-filing is characterised as fraud, leading to imprisonment (5 years) and fine (€500,000). A judge may order restitution of wrongly distributed profits and a ban on company management for up to 15 years.

stage_6.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell company can be held personally liable for the taxes of the legal entity if they used the company as a conduit for a fraud scheme (especially under Article L 267 of the Book of Tax Procedures: liability of directors for tax debts when the company committed tax fraud). The court may additionally impose travel bans, professional bans, confiscation of personal assets and a personal criminal fine. If the director is a foreign resident of a treaty country, the Ministry of Justice may request his or her extradition or enforce French criminal sanctions, and, where convicted, the personal sentence can include the order to reside (interdiction de séjour) in France for up to 10 years.
